reason: The wet methane stream needs to be stored dry and cold, so the methane liquefier seems like a useful place to start.
expectation: I expect the plant to dry and liquefy the methane for storage, though I don't know whether this single step will complete the goal.

alternatives.reason: Storing oxygen is also a stated goal, but I chose to handle the methane stream first.

effect: The methane store is working, so the remaining stated goal is to store the oxygen separately.
reaction: It is satisfying to see the methane collected, though the months needed for production make the wait clear.
reason: The oxygen liquefier is the only available combination and directly addresses the remaining goal.
expectation: I expect the oxygen to be liquefied and collected in its own store, though I don't know whether that will complete the chapter.

effect: The oxygen is now in its own compatible store, completing both goals and establishing the beginning of a way off Mars.
reaction: The separate stores make the distinction between methane fuel and oxygen oxidizer clear, though both actions felt predictable.

mostWorthwhile.text: Storing the wet methane was most worthwhile because it showed that residual water must be removed before liquefaction and that production will take months.

leastWorthwhile.text: Storing the oxygen was straightforward and was the only remaining combination, so it offered little decision-making.

surprise.text: I was struck by how long the stores will take to fill, even though the first liquid has already collected.

arbitrary.text: Neither action felt arbitrary; each matched a stated storage goal and its corresponding liquefier.

continue.text: Yes. I would continue to see how the long production period and the effort to bring the specimens home unfold, although this chapter offered few choices.
